messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — multiple 502/504s reported across eu-rt gateways (region: eu-west). Severity: P1. Summary: spike in gateway errors + increased tail latency. Paging on-call: @Maya SRE. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-452

Maya SRE: seeing ~12% 5xx on prod-eu for inference endpoints. Latency tails up to 3s on small requests. Noting a big rise in KV cache miss rate in telemetry.

Jared (runtime): confirm — runtime metrics show prefix-cache miss-rate jumped 18x at 10:41 UTC. Eviction rate also spiked, lots of 'cache invalidation' logs. Possible cascading flush across shards.

Maya SRE: collecting traces now. Reproducing a 502 from gateway: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` + upstream timeout in router logs.

Emily (platform): I see autoscaler triggered new node spinups but many requests still hit 502 before new capacity came online. Could be a hot-spot on specific prefix shards.

Maya SRE: attaching a short log tail from one affected node:```[2026-02-22T10:40:59Z] prefix-cache: shard-17 eviction triggered: reason=heartbeat-mismatch, entries_evicted=8243
[2026-02-22T10:41:01Z] prefix-cache: miss-rate now 0.72 -> backend reads spiked
[2026-02-22T10:41:05Z] kv-store: checksum-mismatch detected for prefix idx 0x3fa2
[2026-02-22T10:41:06Z] router: upstream timeout 1.5s -> returning 502
```

Rachel Support: customer-impact: multiple paid customers in EU reported degraded API responses. Rachel is drafting an initial customer message. ETA on mitigation?

Maya SRE: mitigation plan options: 1) disable aggressive prefetch for prefix-cache (cheap, quick) 2) force-readthrough to cold KV (increases tail cost but reduces cache pressure) 3) route traffic to fallback pool (if capacity available).

Dennis Pager: prioritize fast mitigations to stop user-facing 5xx. Action: do (1) now, then (2) if errors persist. @Jared can you push a temporary config?

Jared (runtime): preparing rollout: config key `runtime.cache.prefetch.enabled` -> false for prod-eu. Will push a canary to 10% then 100% if green. Command to apply:```curl -XPOST https://config.redwood.internal/v1/apps/runtime/prod-eu -d '{"runtime.cache.prefetch.enabled": false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'```

Maya SRE: canary at 10% live. Monitoring logs…

deploy-bot: deploy started by Jared (runtime) — change id cfg-20260222-07 — canary 10% -> 10% nodes (eu-west).

Maya SRE: after canary: 5xx rate in canary cohort dropped to 1.2% from 12%. Non-canary still high. Good sign. Proceed to full rollout?

Jared (runtime): rolling to 100% now. ETA ~60s for control plane to propagate.

deploy-bot: rollout complete for cfg-20260222-07 — 100% nodes.

Maya SRE: immediate drop in global 5xx to ~2.5%, tail latency decreased. But some residual errors from nodes with eviction backlog; working on draining.

Emily (platform): kicked off a targeted drain/restart for 6 affected worker pods in shard-range 16-20 to clear corrupted in-memory index. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-worker -l shard=16..20 -n prod-eu`

Jared (runtime): also enabling a bypass policy for the router to prefer healthy shards: `router.policy.prefers_healthy=true` (hotfix). Will revert after stabilization.

Maya SRE: executing readthrough fallback if we see cache checksum mismatch. Hook added to crash-loop-protect: `if checksum_mismatch -> readthrough=true`

Rachel Support: sent customer update: "We're investigating elevated 5xx in EU, mitigation in progress, next update in 30m." Customers asked about data corruption — can we confirm?

Jared (runtime): initial forensic: one node had corrupted index due to an earlier kernel OOM/reclaim event during GC window coinciding with prefetch bursts. That caused a shard-level eviction cascade when heartbeat reconciler marked it stale. We're seeing checksum mismatches on a small fraction (<0.02%) of keys; KV store fallback readthrough returns correct values. No durable data loss.

Dennis Pager: good — prioritize full verification sweep. Action items: Maya to confirm global 5xx <1% sustained. Jared to run checksum sweep and publish list of affected shards. Emily to coordinate pod restarts and capacity to avoid re-trigger. Rachel to update customers. I'll hold handoff in 30m.

Maya SRE: monitoring shows 5xx at 0.7% over last 5m, error budgets stable. I'll keep the pager loop open until 11:30 UTC.

Jared (runtime): running checksum-scan job: `./tools/kv-checksum-scan --shards=16-20 --concurrency=8 --output=/tmp/checksum-20260222.csv` — starting now. Will attach results.

Emily (platform): added a temporary rate-limit on aggressive prefetch traffic: `prefetch.qps_cap=1200` for prod-eu to avoid surge.

Rachel Support: sent follow-up to customers explaining root cause suspected, mitigation applied, and that we have no evidence of persistent data loss. Will provide a post-incident update once checks complete.

Maya SRE: handoff note for next oncall: monitor `prefix-cache.miss_rate` and `kv.checksum_mismatch.count`. If either rises >0.5% above baseline, escalate to runtime lead.

Dennis Pager: handing to next oncall @Maya SRE -> @Dennis Pager in 30m. Closing initial P1 dialing down to P2 for verification. Thanks team :thumbsup:
